      Natural Language Statement

      Definition

      A result on a scheduling problem is a statement about its decision version on words, about algorithms that output schedules, or about online play. Such statements depend on how instances and schedules are written, so they are made relative to a reading of the problem: which words encode which instance, which words write which schedule, and what an online scheduler sees at each time. A reading of a family gives one for every specification. The results of the literature are claims about the standard binary readings; here every result is a proposition about a given reading.

      Fix a reading and parameters κ\kappaκ: functions of the instance and the threshold into the naturals (most depend on the instance only; some, such as the pathwidth of time windows that end at the threshold, depend on both). The decision version on words: a word of an instance, then the sign and absolute value of an integral threshold DDD, is a yes-instance if some feasible schedule has cost at most DDD. Running times are those of the word RAM (lax-496464, lax-808846).

      Exact algorithms and hardness. In P: decided in time c (∣w∣+1)dc\,(|w|+1)^dc(∣w∣+1)d in the bit size ∣w∣|w|∣w∣. Pseudo-polynomial: in time c (M+1)e(∣w∣+1)dc\,(M+1)^e(|w|+1)^dc(M+1)e(∣w∣+1)d, where MMM is the largest number of the word. NP-hard: NPHardInNPHardInNPHardIn of lax-496464; strongly NP-hard: NP-hard on the words whose numbers are at most c (length+1)dc\,(\text{length}+1)^dc(length+1)d. In P (pseudo-polynomial) for every fixed value of κ\kappaκ; FPT, W[t]-hard (strongly: on such words), para-NP-hard: NP-hard for one fixed value.

      Running times. An algorithm can be stated with its exact running time, a function TTT of the instance (of nnn, mmm, pmax⁡p_{\max}pmax​, the total weight, …): one program halts, writing the answer for the instance and the threshold, within c (T(x)+1)c\,(T(x)+1)c(T(x)+1) instructions on the word of every instance xxx, at every word length ℓ\ellℓ with (∣w∣+M+2)c≤2ℓ(|w| + M + 2)^c \le 2^\ell(∣w∣+M+2)c≤2ℓ, where ∣w∣|w|∣w∣ is the length of the word and MMM its largest number — words of O(log⁡)O(\log)O(log) bits, as on the word RAM of the literature. Deciding, approximating, approximating with random bits and approximation schemes each have such a form; a submitted algorithm is a program with a proof of one of them. Deciding can also be stated without the constant: one program halts with the answer within exactly T(x,D)T(x, D)T(x,D) instructions, a function of the instance and the threshold, at the same word lengths.

      Randomized deciding. The program reads, after the word, at most c (T(x)+1)c\,(T(x)+1)c(T(x)+1) random bits and halts within c (T(x)+1)c\,(T(x)+1)c(T(x)+1) instructions on every choice of them. With bounded error its answer is right for at least two thirds of the choices. With one-sided error it never accepts a no-instance and accepts a yes-instance for at least half of the choices. With zero error (Las Vegas) it is always right and the bound c (T(x)+1)c\,(T(x)+1)c(T(x)+1) holds for the number of instructions averaged over the choices. Repetition turns any of these into error 2−k2^{-k}2−k at kkk times the cost, so the constants 2/32/32/3 and 1/21/21/2 are not essential.

      Approximation. A ratio is a function ρ\rhoρ of the instance into the reals. A ρ\rhoρ-approximation is a polynomial-time program that on the word of an instance with a feasible schedule writes the word of a feasible schedule costing at most ρ\rhoρ times every feasible schedule; for a maximization problem, whose cost is the negative of its value, the value is at least ρ\rhoρ times every value. A randomized one reads polynomially many random bits; every choice gives a feasible schedule, the average cost is within the ratio, and the running time is polynomial in the worst case or, for an expected-time algorithm, on average over the bits. Approximations may be restricted to the instances of a set. PTAS, EPTAS and FPTAS are as usual; inapproximability below ρ\rhoρ unless P = NP says that if P ≠ NP no ρ′\rho'ρ′-approximation exists for a constant ρ′<ρ\rho' < \rhoρ′<ρ. An *additive* δ\deltaδ-approximation writes a feasible schedule costing at most every feasible cost plus δ\deltaδ, a function of the instance; an additive scheme does so with ε δ\varepsilon\,\deltaεδ for every ε>0\varepsilon > 0ε>0, in polynomial time for each fixed ε\varepsilonε. A parameterized approximation scheme for a parameter κ\kappaκ is one program that writes a (1+a/b)(1 + a/b)(1+a/b)-approximate schedule from the word of an instance followed by a,ba, ba,b, in time f(κ+b/a) (∣w∣+1)df(\kappa + b/a)\,(|w|+1)^df(κ+b/a)(∣w∣+1)d.

      Running times and word size. A running time, upper or lower, is stated with short words, ℓ≥clog⁡2(∣u∣+M+2)\ell \ge c \log_2(|u| + M + 2)ℓ≥clog2​(∣u∣+M+2); the classes keep the long words of the registered notions and are reached from running times through the transfer theorems. A lower bound is stated for the time plus the length of the shortest word of the instance.

      Wide words. An algorithm whose running time TTT exceeds every polynomial may need words that hold the address of every step, c (T(x)+1)≤2ℓc\,(T(x)+1) \le 2^\ellc(T(x)+1)≤2ℓ besides the short words above; this is the standard assumption for such algorithms, whose tables are as large as their running times. Deciding within O(T)O(T)O(T) with wide words asks the program to work only at those word lengths.

      Restrictions. A result may hold on the instances satisfying a predicate φ\varphiφ only: it is then a result on the problem restricted to them, read with the same words.

      Kept weight. A problem that minimizes the weight of the jobs it rejects (late, or not just in time) is read with the same instances, schedules and costs when a source maximizes the weight it keeps. The kept weight of a schedule is the total weight WWW of the instance minus its cost. A ρ\rhoρ-approximation of the kept weight, for ρ≤1\rho \le 1ρ≤1, writes a feasible schedule that keeps at least ρ\rhoρ times the weight of every feasible schedule; schemes keep 1−a/b1 - a/b1−a/b times it. An online algorithm is ρ\rhoρ-competitive for the kept weight, ρ≥1\rho \ge 1ρ≥1, if every feasible schedule keeps at most ρ\rhoρ times what the algorithm keeps plus a constant, the convention of the sources on throughput.

      Kernels. A kernelization for a parameter is a polynomial-time map on the words of instances that keeps the answer and whose output has size (bit length) and parameter at most g(κ)g(\kappa)g(κ) for a computable ggg; a polynomial kernel has ggg polynomial.

      The exponential time hypothesis. A formula is written as the number nnn of variables followed, for every clause, by its length and its literals, the literal of variable vvv being 2v+12v+12v+1 if positive and 2v2v2v if negative. ETH: for some q>0q > 0q>0 no program decides the satisfiability of formulas whose clauses have three literals over variables below nnn within c 2⌊n/q⌋(∣w∣+1)cc\,2^{\lfloor n/q \rfloor}(|w|+1)^cc2⌊n/q⌋(∣w∣+1)c instructions, at the word lengths above. A function fff is o(g)o(g)o(g) if for every rational ε>0\varepsilon > 0ε>0, eventually f(k)≤ε g(k)f(k) \le \varepsilon\, g(k)f(k)≤εg(k).

      Online. A deterministic algorithm is ρ\rhoρ-competitive if it is non-anticipative for the revelation and, for some additive constant, its cost is at most ρ\rhoρ times every feasible cost plus that constant; a randomized one is a finite distribution over non-anticipative algorithms. A lower bound ρ\rhoρ says that no algorithm is ρ′\rho'ρ′-competitive for ρ′<ρ\rho' < \rhoρ′<ρ.

      132/-- Parameterized problems on words. -/
      133abbrev WP := Lax888481.ParameterizedComplexity.Problem
      134
      135/-- A reading of a problem: words of instances, schedules from words, and what
      136an online scheduler sees. -/
      137structure PReading (P : Problem) where
      138 /-- The word encodes the instance. -/
      139 Encodes : List ℕ → P.Inst → Prop
      140 /-- The word writes the schedule of the instance. -/
      141 Decodes : (x : P.Inst) → List ℕ → P.Sched x → Prop
      142 /-- What is revealed over time. -/
      143 reveal : Revelation P
      144
      145/-- A reading of a family. -/
      146structure Reading {K : Kernel} (F : Family K) where
      147 /-- The word encodes the instance. -/
      148 Encodes : (s : Spec F) → List ℕ → Inst F s → Prop
      149 /-- The word writes the schedule of the instance. -/
      150 Decodes : (s : Spec F) → (x : Inst F s) → List ℕ → (problem F s).Sched x → Prop
      151 /-- What is revealed over time. -/
      152 reveal : (s : Spec F) → Revelation (problem F s)
      153
      154/-- The reading of the problem of one specification. -/
      155def Reading.at {K : Kernel} {F : Family K} (R : Reading F) (s : Spec F) :
      156 PReading (problem F s) :=
      157 ⟨R.Encodes s, R.Decodes s, R.reveal s⟩
      158
      159/-- The reading of a problem on the instances satisfying `φ`: the same words. -/
      160def PReading.restrict {P : Problem} (R : PReading P) (φ : P.Inst → Prop) :
      161 PReading (P.restrict φ) where
      162 Encodes w x := R.Encodes w x.1
      163 Decodes x w σ := R.Decodes x.1 w σ
      164 reveal := ⟨fun x y t => R.reveal.same x.1 y.1 t, fun x y σ τ t => R.reveal.agree x.1 y.1 σ τ t⟩
      165
      166/-- A parameter of the decision version: a function of the instance and the
      167threshold. -/
      168abbrev TParameter (P : Problem) := P.Inst → ℤ → ℕ
      169
      170/-- A parameter of the instance, ignoring the threshold. -/
      171def lift {P : Problem} (κ : Parameter P) : TParameter P := fun x _ => κ x
      172
      173/-- The sum of two parameters. -/
      174def tplus {P : Problem} (κ κ' : TParameter P) : TParameter P := fun x D => κ x D + κ' x D
      175
      176variable {P : Problem} (R : PReading P)
      177
      178-- Words
      179
      180/-- The largest number of a word. -/
      181def maxEntry (w : List ℕ) : ℕ := w.foldr max 0
      182
      183/-- The word presents the instance with the threshold. -/
      184def EncodesDecision (w : List ℕ) (x : P.Inst) (D : ℤ) : Prop :=
      185 ∃ y, w = y ++ [if D < 0 then 1 else 0, D.natAbs] ∧ R.Encodes y x
      186
      187open Classical in
      188/-- The decision version with a parameter, as a parameterized problem on words. -/
      189noncomputable def parameterized (κ : TParameter P) : WP where
      190 Domain := {w | ∃ x D, EncodesDecision R w x D}
      191 Yes w := ∃ x D, EncodesDecision R w x D ∧ P.Decides x D
      192 param w := if h : ∃ x D, EncodesDecision R w x D then κ h.choose h.choose_spec.choose else 0
      193
      194/-- The decision version on words. -/
      195noncomputable def decision : WP := parameterized R fun _ => 0
      196
      197open Classical in
      198/-- The answer of a word, `[1]` or `[0]`. -/
      199noncomputable def answer (Q : WP) (w : List ℕ) : List ℕ := if Q.Yes w then [1] else [0]
      200
      201/-- The problem on fewer words. -/
      202def restrict (Q : WP) (D : Set (List ℕ)) : WP where
      203 Domain := Q.Domain ∩ D
      204 Yes := Q.Yes
      205 param := Q.param
      206
      207/-- The words whose numbers are polynomial in their length. -/
      208def Small (c d : ℕ) : Set (List ℕ) := {w | ∀ v ∈ w, v ≤ c * (w.length + 1) ^ d}
      209
      210/-- The words of instances with parameter at most `k`. -/
      211def Upto (κ : TParameter P) (k : ℕ) : Set (List ℕ) :=
      212 {w | ∃ x D, EncodesDecision R w x D ∧ κ x D ≤ k}
      213
      214-- Exact algorithms and hardness
      215
      216/-- Decided in polynomial time. -/
      217def PolyDecides (Q : WP) : Prop := PolyTimeOn Q.Domain (answer Q)
      218
      219/-- Decided in pseudo-polynomial time. -/
      220def PseudoPolyDecides (Q : WP) : Prop :=
      221 ∃ (p : Program) (c e d : ℕ),
      222 ComputesInFptTime p Q.Domain maxEntry (answer Q) (fun k => c * (k + 1) ^ e) d
      223
      224/-- The problem is in P. -/
      225def InP : Prop := PolyDecides (decision R)
      226
      227/-- The problem is solvable in pseudo-polynomial time. -/
      228def PseudoPoly : Prop := PseudoPolyDecides (decision R)
      229
      230/-- The problem is NP-hard. -/
      231def NPHard : Prop := Lax496464.WH_F3_NPHard.NPHardIn (decision R)
      232
      233/-- The problem is strongly NP-hard. -/
      234def StronglyNPHard : Prop :=
      235 ∃ c d, Lax496464.WH_F3_NPHard.NPHardIn (restrict (decision R) (Small c d))
      236
      237/-- In P for every fixed value of the parameter. -/
      238def InPFixed (κ : TParameter P) : Prop :=
      239 ∀ k, PolyDecides (restrict (decision R) (Upto R κ k))
      240
      241/-- Pseudo-polynomial for every fixed value of the parameter. -/
      242def PseudoPolyFixed (κ : TParameter P) : Prop :=
      243 ∀ k, PseudoPolyDecides (restrict (decision R) (Upto R κ k))
      244
      245/-- Fixed-parameter tractable. -/
      246def IsFPT (κ : TParameter P) : Prop := parameterized R κ ∈ FPT
      247
      248/-- W[t]-hard. -/
      249def WHard (t : ℕ) (κ : TParameter P) : Prop := Hard (W t) (parameterized R κ)
      250
      251/-- Strongly W[t]-hard: W[t]-hard on the words whose numbers are polynomial in
      252their length. -/
      253def StronglyWHard (t : ℕ) (κ : TParameter P) : Prop :=
      254 ∃ c d, Hard (W t) (restrict (parameterized R κ) (Small c d))
      255
      256/-- Para-NP-hard: NP-hard for one fixed value of the parameter. -/
      257def ParaNPHard (κ : TParameter P) : Prop :=
      258 ∃ k, Lax496464.WH_F3_NPHard.NPHardIn (restrict (decision R) (Upto R κ k))
      259
      260/-- Strongly NP-hard for one fixed value of the parameter. -/
      261def StronglyParaNPHard (κ : TParameter P) : Prop :=
      262 ∃ k c d, Lax496464.WH_F3_NPHard.NPHardIn
      263 (restrict (decision R) (Upto R κ k ∩ Small c d))
      264
      265-- Approximation
      266
      267open Classical in
      268/-- The length of the shortest word of the instance, `0` if it has none. Lower
      269bounds on running times are stated for a time plus this length, so that they
      270cannot hold just because the input cannot be read. -/
      271noncomputable def inputSize (x : P.Inst) : ℕ := sInf {k | ∃ w, R.Encodes w x ∧ w.length = k}
      272
      273/-- The instance has a feasible schedule. -/
      274def Solvable (x : P.Inst) : Prop := ∃ τ, P.feasible x τ
      275
      276/-- `σ` is feasible and within the ratio of every feasible schedule. -/
      277def Within (ρ : ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (σ : P.Sched x) : Prop :=
      278 P.feasible x σ ∧ ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ → (P.cost x σ : ℝ) ≤ ρ * P.cost x τ
      279
      280/-- For a maximization problem: `σ` is feasible and its value is at least `ρ`
      281times every value. -/
      282def WithinMax (ρ : ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (σ : P.Sched x) : Prop :=
      283 P.feasible x σ ∧ ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ → ρ * (-(P.cost x τ : ℝ)) ≤ -(P.cost x σ : ℝ)
      284
      285/-- The output word, read on instance `x`, is a schedule within the ratio. -/
      286def Good (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (out : List ℕ) : Prop :=
      287 ∃ σ, R.Decodes x out σ ∧ Within (ρ x) x σ
      288
      289/-- The same for a maximization problem. -/
      290def GoodMax (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (out : List ℕ) : Prop :=
      291 ∃ σ, R.Decodes x out σ ∧ WithinMax (ρ x) x σ
      292
      293/-- All instances. -/
      294def univ : Set P.Inst := Set.univ
      295
      296/-- A constant ratio. -/
      297def const (ρ : ℝ) : P.Inst → ℝ := fun _ => ρ
      298
      299/-- A polynomial-time `ρ`-approximation on the instances of `S`. -/
      300def ApproxOn (S : Set P.Inst) (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
      301 ∃ A : List ℕ → List ℕ, PolyTimeOn {w | ∃ x ∈ S, R.Encodes w x} A ∧
      302 ∀ w x, R.Encodes w x → x ∈ S → Solvable x → Good R ρ x (A w)
      303
      304/-- A polynomial-time `ρ`-approximation. -/
      305def Approx (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop := ApproxOn R univ ρ
      306
      307/-- A polynomial-time `ρ`-approximation for a maximization problem. -/
      308def ApproxMax (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
      309 ∃ A : List ℕ → List ℕ, PolyTimeOn {w | ∃ x, R.Encodes w x} A ∧
      310 ∀ w x, R.Encodes w x → Solvable x → GoodMax R ρ x (A w)
      311
      312/-- A polynomial-time `ρ`-approximation for every fixed value of the parameter. -/
      313def ApproxFixed (κ : Parameter P) (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
      314 ∀ k, ApproxOn R {x | κ x ≤ k} ρ
      315
      316/-- The random bits `r` as a word. -/
      317def bits {L : ℕ} (r : Fin L → Bool) : List ℕ := List.ofFn fun i => if r i then 1 else 0
      318
      319/-- Every choice of the random bits gives a feasible schedule, and the average
      320cost is within the ratio. -/
      321def GoodOnAverage {L : ℕ} (ρ : ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (out : (Fin L → Bool) → List ℕ) : Prop :=
      322 ∃ σ : (Fin L → Bool) → P.Sched x,
      323 (∀ r, R.Decodes x (out r) (σ r) ∧ P.feasible x (σ r)) ∧
      324 ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ → (∑ r, (P.cost x (σ r) : ℝ)) / 2 ^ L ≤ ρ * P.cost x τ
      325
      326/-- A randomized polynomial-time `ρ`-approximation: it reads `L(|w|)` random
      327bits, with `L` polynomial, and runs in polynomial time on every choice. -/
      328def RandomApprox (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
      329 ∃ (A : List ℕ → List ℕ) (L : ℕ → ℕ) (c e : ℕ), (∀ n, L n ≤ c * (n + 1) ^ e) ∧
      330 PolyTimeOn {u | ∃ w x, R.Encodes w x ∧ ∃ r : Fin (L (bitSize w)) → Bool, u = w ++ bits r} A ∧
      331 ∀ w x, R.Encodes w x → Solvable x →
      332 GoodOnAverage R (ρ x) x fun r : Fin (L (bitSize w)) → Bool => A (w ++ bits r)
      333
      334/-- The word lengths a program may use on input `u`: `c` times the logarithm of
      335the length plus the largest number. -/
      336def WordOk (c : ℕ) (u : List ℕ) (ℓ : ℕ) : Prop := (u.length + maxEntry u + 2) ^ c ≤ 2 ^ ℓ
      337
      338/-- A randomized `ρ`-approximation in expected polynomial time: averaged over
      339the random bits, the number of instructions is at most `c (|w|+1)^c`. -/
      340def RandomApproxExpected (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
      341 ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ) (L : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, L n ≤ c * (n + 1) ^ c) ∧
      342 ∀ w x, R.Encodes w x → Solvable x →
      343 ∃ out : (Fin (L w.length) → Bool) → List ℕ, GoodOnAverage R (ρ x) x out ∧
      344 ∀ ℓ, (∀ r : Fin (L w.length) → Bool, WordOk c (w ++ bits r) ℓ) →
      345 ∃ t : (Fin (L w.length) → Bool) → ℕ,
      346 (∀ r, RunsTo ℓ p ((w ++ bits r).length :: (w ++ bits r)) (out r) (t r)) ∧
      347 (∑ r, (t r : ℝ)) / 2 ^ L w.length ≤ c * (w.length + 1 : ℝ) ^ c
      348
      349/-- A polynomial-time approximation scheme. -/
      350def PTAS : Prop := ∀ ε : ℚ, 0 < ε → Approx R (const (1 + ε))
      351
      352/-- A PTAS for a maximization problem: value at least `1 - ε` times every
      353value. -/
      354def PTASMax : Prop := ∀ ε : ℚ, 0 < ε → ε < 1 → ApproxMax R (const (1 - ε))
      355
      356/-- A PTAS for every fixed value of the parameter. -/
      357def PTASFixed (κ : Parameter P) : Prop :=
      358 ∀ k (ε : ℚ), 0 < ε → ApproxOn R {x | κ x ≤ k} (const (1 + ε))
      359
      360/-- The words of instances followed by a precision `a / b`. -/
      361def WordsEps : Set (List ℕ) :=
      362 {u | ∃ w x, R.Encodes w x ∧ ∃ a b, 0 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧ u = w ++ [a, b]}
      363
      364/-- One program writes a `(1 + a / b)`-approximate schedule from the word of an
      365instance followed by `a, b`. -/
      366def Scheme (A : List ℕ → List ℕ) : Prop :=
      367 ∀ w x (a b : ℕ), R.Encodes w x → 0 < a → 0 < b → Solvable x →
      368 Good R (const (1 + (a : ℝ) / b)) x (A (w ++ [a, b]))
      369
      370/-- An efficient PTAS: time `f(b/a) · (|w|+1)^d`. -/
      371def EPTAS : Prop :=
      372 ∃ A, Scheme R A ∧ FptTimeOn (WordsEps R) (fun u => u.getLastD 0 / u.dropLast.getLastD 1 + 1) A
      373
      374/-- A fully polynomial-time approximation scheme: time polynomial in `|w|` and
      375`b/a`. -/
      376def FPTAS : Prop :=
      377 ∃ A, Scheme R A ∧ ∃ (p : Program) (c e d : ℕ), ComputesInFptTime p (WordsEps R)
      378 (fun u => u.getLastD 0 / u.dropLast.getLastD 1 + 1) A (fun k => c * (k + 1) ^ e) d
      379
      380/-- P ≠ NP. -/
      381def PneNP : Prop :=
      382 Lax434930.PolynomialTime.P ≠ Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime.NP
      383
      384/-- No `ρ'`-approximation for a constant `ρ' < ρ` on the instances of `S`,
      385unless P = NP. -/
      386def NoApproxBelowOn (S : Set P.Inst) (ρ : ℝ) : Prop :=
      387 PneNP → ∀ ρ' : ℝ, ρ' < ρ → ¬ ApproxOn R S (const ρ')
      388
      389/-- No `ρ'`-approximation for a constant `ρ' < ρ`, unless P = NP. -/
      390def NoApproxBelow (ρ : ℝ) : Prop := NoApproxBelowOn R univ ρ
      391
      392/-- No PTAS unless P = NP (the consequence of APX-hardness). -/
      393def NoPTAS : Prop := PneNP → ¬ PTAS R
      394
      395/-- `σ` is feasible and costs at most every feasible cost plus `δ`. -/
      396def WithinAdd (δ : ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (σ : P.Sched x) : Prop :=
      397 P.feasible x σ ∧ ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ → (P.cost x σ : ℝ) ≤ P.cost x τ + δ
      398
      399/-- The output word, read on instance `x`, is a schedule within the additive error. -/
      400def GoodAdd (δ : P.Inst → ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (out : List ℕ) : Prop :=
      401 ∃ σ, R.Decodes x out σ ∧ WithinAdd (δ x) x σ
      402
      403/-- A polynomial-time approximation with additive error `δ`. -/
      404def ApproxAdd (δ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
      405 ∃ A : List ℕ → List ℕ, PolyTimeOn {w | ∃ x, R.Encodes w x} A ∧
      406 ∀ w x, R.Encodes w x → Solvable x → GoodAdd R δ x (A w)
      407
      408/-- An additive approximation scheme: additive error `ε δ` for every `ε > 0`, in polynomial
      409time for each fixed `ε`. -/
      410def AddScheme (δ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop := ∀ ε : ℚ, 0 < ε → ApproxAdd R fun x => (ε : ℝ) * δ x
      411
      412open Classical in
      413/-- The parameter of the instance a word followed by a precision writes, plus the inverse
      414precision `b / a`. -/
      415noncomputable def paramEps (κ : Parameter P) (u : List ℕ) : ℕ :=
      416 (if h : ∃ x, R.Encodes (u.dropLast.dropLast) x then κ h.choose else 0) +
      417 u.getLastD 0 / u.dropLast.getLastD 1 + 1
      418
      419/-- A parameterized approximation scheme: time `f(κ + b/a) · (|w|+1)^d`. -/
      420def ParamScheme (κ : Parameter P) : Prop :=
      421 ∃ A, Scheme R A ∧ FptTimeOn (WordsEps R) (paramEps R κ) A
      422
      423/-- A kernelization: a polynomial-time map on the words of instances with a threshold that
      424keeps the answer and the words, and whose output has size and parameter at most `g κ`. -/
      425def KernelWithin (κ : TParameter P) (g : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
      426 ∃ K : List ℕ → List ℕ, PolyTimeOn (parameterized R κ).Domain K ∧
      427 ∀ w ∈ (parameterized R κ).Domain, K w ∈ (parameterized R κ).Domain ∧
      428 ((parameterized R κ).Yes w ↔ (parameterized R κ).Yes (K w)) ∧
      429 bitSize (K w) ≤ g ((parameterized R κ).param w) ∧
      430 (parameterized R κ).param (K w) ≤ g ((parameterized R κ).param w)
      431
      432/-- A kernel: a kernelization for a computable `g`. -/
      433def HasKernel (κ : TParameter P) : Prop := ∃ g, Computable g ∧ KernelWithin R κ g
      434
      435/-- A polynomial kernel: a kernelization with `g` polynomial. -/
      436def PolyKernel (κ : TParameter P) : Prop := ∃ c d : ℕ, KernelWithin R κ fun k => c * (k + 1) ^ d
      437
      438-- Kept weight
      439
      440/-- `σ` is feasible and keeps at least `ρ` times the weight every feasible
      441schedule keeps, the kept weight being the total weight minus the cost. -/
      442def WithinKept (total : Parameter P) (ρ : ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (σ : P.Sched x) : Prop :=
      443 P.feasible x σ ∧ ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ →
      444 ρ * ((total x : ℝ) - P.cost x τ) ≤ (total x : ℝ) - P.cost x σ
      445
      446/-- The output word, read on instance `x`, is a schedule within the ratio of
      447the kept weight. -/
      448def GoodKept (total : Parameter P) (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) (x : P.Inst) (out : List ℕ) : Prop :=
      449 ∃ σ, R.Decodes x out σ ∧ WithinKept total (ρ x) x σ
      450
      451/-- A polynomial-time `ρ`-approximation of the kept weight, `ρ ≤ 1`. -/
      452def ApproxKept (total : Parameter P) (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
      453 ∃ A : List ℕ → List ℕ, PolyTimeOn {w | ∃ x, R.Encodes w x} A ∧
      454 ∀ w x, R.Encodes w x → Solvable x → GoodKept R total ρ x (A w)
      455
      456/-- One program keeps `1 - a / b` times the optimal kept weight, from the word
      457of an instance followed by `a, b` with `a < b`. -/
      458def SchemeKept (total : Parameter P) (A : List ℕ → List ℕ) : Prop :=
      459 ∀ w x (a b : ℕ), R.Encodes w x → 0 < a → a < b → Solvable x →
      460 GoodKept R total (const (1 - (a : ℝ) / b)) x (A (w ++ [a, b]))
      461
      462/-- A PTAS for the kept weight. -/
      463def PTASKept (total : Parameter P) : Prop :=
      464 ∀ ε : ℚ, 0 < ε → ε < 1 → ApproxKept R total (const (1 - ε))
      465
      466/-- An efficient PTAS for the kept weight: time `f(b/a) · (|w|+1)^d`. -/
      467def EPTASKept (total : Parameter P) : Prop :=
      468 ∃ A, SchemeKept R total A ∧
      469 FptTimeOn (WordsEps R) (fun u => u.getLastD 0 / u.dropLast.getLastD 1 + 1) A
      470
      471/-- An FPTAS for the kept weight: time polynomial in `|w|` and `b/a`. -/
      472def FPTASKept (total : Parameter P) : Prop :=
      473 ∃ A, SchemeKept R total A ∧ ∃ (p : Program) (c e d : ℕ), ComputesInFptTime p (WordsEps R)
      474 (fun u => u.getLastD 0 / u.dropLast.getLastD 1 + 1) A (fun k => c * (k + 1) ^ e) d
      475
      476/-- A parameterized approximation scheme for the kept weight. -/
      477def ParamSchemeKept (total : Parameter P) (κ : Parameter P) : Prop :=
      478 ∃ A, SchemeKept R total A ∧ FptTimeOn (WordsEps R) (paramEps R κ) A
      479
      480/-- No `ρ'`-approximation of the kept weight for a constant `ρ' > ρ`, unless
      481P = NP. -/
      482def NoApproxKeptAbove (total : Parameter P) (ρ : ℝ) : Prop :=
      483 PneNP → ∀ ρ' : ℝ, ρ < ρ' → ¬ ApproxKept R total (const ρ')
      484
      485-- Running times
      486
      487open Classical in
      488/-- The answer for an instance and a threshold: `[1]` if some feasible schedule
      489costs at most the threshold, `[0]` otherwise. -/
      490noncomputable def verdict (x : P.Inst) (D : ℤ) : List ℕ := if P.Decides x D then [1] else [0]
      491
      492/-- One program decides the decision version within `O(T(x))` instructions: on
      493every word of an instance `x` with a threshold `D` it writes the answer for `x`
      494and `D`. -/
      495def DecidesWithin (T : P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
      496 ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ), ∀ u x D, EncodesDecision R u x D →
      497 ∀ ℓ, WordOk c u ℓ → ∃ t ≤ c * (T x + 1),
      498 RunsTo ℓ p (u.length :: u) (verdict x D) t
      499
      500/-- One program decides the decision version within `T x D` instructions, with no
      501hidden constant: on every word of an instance `x` with a threshold `D` it writes the
      502answer within `T x D` steps of the word RAM. -/
      503def DecidesExact (T : P.Inst → ℤ → ℕ) : Prop :=
      504 ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ), ∀ u x D, EncodesDecision R u x D →
      505 ∀ ℓ, WordOk c u ℓ → ∃ t ≤ T x D, RunsTo ℓ p (u.length :: u) (verdict x D) t
      506
      507/-- One program decides the decision version within `O(T(x))` instructions with wide
      508words: on every word of an instance `x` with a threshold `D`, at every word length `ℓ` with
      509`WordOk c u ℓ` and `c (T(x) + 1) ≤ 2 ^ ℓ`, it writes the answer for `x` and `D` within
      510`c (T(x) + 1)` instructions. This is the standard assumption for algorithms whose running
      511time exceeds a polynomial: a word holds the address of every step. -/
      512def DecidesWithinWide (T : P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
      513 ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ), ∀ u x D, EncodesDecision R u x D →
      514 ∀ ℓ, WordOk c u ℓ → c * (T x + 1) ≤ 2 ^ ℓ → ∃ t ≤ c * (T x + 1),
      515 RunsTo ℓ p (u.length :: u) (verdict x D) t
      516
      517open Classical in
      518/-- The choices of `L` random bits for which `out` writes the answer for `x` and `D`. -/
      519noncomputable def rightChoices {L : ℕ} (x : P.Inst) (D : ℤ) (out : (Fin L → Bool) → List ℕ) : ℕ :=
      520 (Finset.univ.filter fun r => out r = verdict x D).card
      521
      522/-- A randomized program decides the decision version with bounded error within
      523`O(T(x))` instructions: on the word of an instance `x` with a threshold `D`
      524followed by at most `O(T(x))` random bits, it halts within `O(T(x))`
      525instructions on every choice, and writes the answer for at least two thirds of
      526the choices. -/
      527def RandomDecidesWithin (T : P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
      528 ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ) (L : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ u x D, EncodesDecision R u x D →
      529 L u.length ≤ c * (T x + 1) ∧
      530 ∃ out : (Fin (L u.length) → Bool) → List ℕ,
      531 2 * 2 ^ L u.length ≤ 3 * rightChoices x D out ∧
      532 ∀ r ℓ, WordOk c (u ++ bits r) ℓ → ∃ t ≤ c * (T x + 1),
      533 RunsTo ℓ p ((u ++ bits r).length :: (u ++ bits r)) (out r) t
      534
      535/-- The same with one-sided error: a no-instance is never accepted, and a
      536yes-instance is accepted for at least half of the choices. -/
      537def OneSidedDecidesWithin (T : P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
      538 ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ) (L : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ u x D, EncodesDecision R u x D →
      539 L u.length ≤ c * (T x + 1) ∧
      540 ∃ out : (Fin (L u.length) → Bool) → List ℕ,
      541 (∀ r, out r = verdict x D ∨ out r = [0]) ∧
      542 2 ^ L u.length ≤ 2 * rightChoices x D out ∧
      543 ∀ r ℓ, WordOk c (u ++ bits r) ℓ → ∃ t ≤ c * (T x + 1),
      544 RunsTo ℓ p ((u ++ bits r).length :: (u ++ bits r)) (out r) t
      545
      546/-- The same with zero error (Las Vegas): the answer is always right, and the
      547number of instructions, averaged over the choices, is `O(T(x))`. -/
      548def ZeroErrorDecidesWithin (T : P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
      549 ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ) (L : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ u x D, EncodesDecision R u x D →
      550 L u.length ≤ c * (T x + 1) ∧
      551 ∀ ℓ, (∀ r : Fin (L u.length) → Bool, WordOk c (u ++ bits r) ℓ) →
      552 ∃ t : (Fin (L u.length) → Bool) → ℕ,
      553 (∀ r, RunsTo ℓ p ((u ++ bits r).length :: (u ++ bits r)) (verdict x D) (t r)) ∧
      554 (∑ r, (t r : ℝ)) / 2 ^ L u.length ≤ c * ((T x : ℝ) + 1)
      555
      556/-- A `ρ`-approximation running within `O(T(x))` instructions. -/
      557def ApproxWithin (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) (T : P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
      558 ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ), ∀ u x, R.Encodes u x → Solvable x →
      559 ∀ ℓ, WordOk c u ℓ → ∃ out, ∃ t ≤ c * (T x + 1),
      560 RunsTo ℓ p (u.length :: u) out t ∧ Good R ρ x out
      561
      562/-- A randomized `ρ`-approximation running within `O(T(x))` instructions on
      563every choice of random bits and reading at most that many. -/
      564def RandomApproxWithin (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) (T : P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
      565 ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ) (L : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ u x, R.Encodes u x → Solvable x →
      566 L u.length ≤ c * (T x + 1) ∧
      567 ∃ out : (Fin (L u.length) → Bool) → List ℕ, GoodOnAverage R (ρ x) x out ∧
      568 ∀ r ℓ, WordOk c (u ++ bits r) ℓ → ∃ t ≤ c * (T x + 1),
      569 RunsTo ℓ p ((u ++ bits r).length :: (u ++ bits r)) (out r) t
      570
      571/-- An approximation scheme: one program reads the word of an instance and `a, b`
      572and writes a `(1 + a/b)`-approximate schedule within `O(T(a/b, x))`
      573instructions. -/
      574def SchemeWithin (T : ℚ → P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
      575 ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ), ∀ u x (a b : ℕ), R.Encodes u x → 0 < a → 0 < b →
      576 Solvable x → ∀ ℓ, WordOk c (u ++ [a, b]) ℓ → ∃ out, ∃ t ≤ c * (T ((a : ℚ) / b) x + 1),
      577 RunsTo ℓ p ((u ++ [a, b]).length :: (u ++ [a, b])) out t ∧
      578 Good R (const (1 + (a : ℝ) / b)) x out
      579
      580/-- The same for a maximization problem: value at least `1 - a/b` times every
      581value, for `a < b`. -/
      582def SchemeMaxWithin (T : ℚ → P.Inst → ℕ) : Prop :=
      583 ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ), ∀ u x (a b : ℕ), R.Encodes u x → 0 < a → a < b →
      584 Solvable x → ∀ ℓ, WordOk c (u ++ [a, b]) ℓ → ∃ out, ∃ t ≤ c * (T ((a : ℚ) / b) x + 1),
      585 RunsTo ℓ p ((u ++ [a, b]).length :: (u ++ [a, b])) out t ∧
      586 GoodMax R (const (1 - (a : ℝ) / b)) x out
      587
      588-- The exponential time hypothesis
      589
      590/-- The word of a formula on `n` variables. -/
      591def formulaWord (n : ℕ) (Φ : Lax429075.CNF.Formula) : List ℕ :=
      592 n :: Φ.flatMap fun C => C.length :: C.map fun l => 2 * l.index + if l.positive then 1 else 0
      593
      594open Classical in
      595/-- The exponential time hypothesis: for some `q > 0`, no program decides 3-SAT
      596on `n` variables within `c · 2^⌊n/q⌋ · (|w|+1)^c` instructions. -/
      597def ETH : Prop :=
      598 ∃ q : ℕ, 0 < q ∧ ∀ (p : Program) (c : ℕ), ¬ ∀ (n : ℕ) (Φ : Lax429075.CNF.Formula),
      599 (∀ C ∈ Φ, C.length = 3 ∧ ∀ l ∈ C, l.index < n) →
      600 ∀ ℓ, WordOk c (formulaWord n Φ) ℓ →
      601 ∃ t ≤ c * 2 ^ (n / q) * ((formulaWord n Φ).length + 1) ^ c,
      602 RunsTo ℓ p ((formulaWord n Φ).length :: formulaWord n Φ)
      603 (if Lax429075.CNF.Satisfiable Φ then [1] else [0]) t
      604
      605/-- `f` is `o(g)`. -/
      606def LittleO (f g : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
      607 ∀ ε : ℚ, 0 < ε → ∃ N, ∀ k ≥ N, (f k : ℚ) ≤ ε * g k
      608
      609-- Online
      610
      611/-- A deterministic algorithm with ratio `ρ` and additive constant `α`, over the
      612reals. -/
      613def CompetitiveR (A : Algorithm P) (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) (α : ℝ) : Prop :=
      614 ∀ x, P.feasible x (A x) ∧ ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ →
      615 (P.cost x (A x) : ℝ) ≤ ρ x * P.cost x τ + α
      616
      617/-- Some non-anticipative deterministic algorithm is `ρ`-competitive. -/
      618def DetCompetitive (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
      619 ∃ A α, NonAnticipative R.reveal A ∧ CompetitiveR A ρ α
      620
      621/-- A distribution over non-anticipative algorithms is `ρ`-competitive. -/
      622def RandCompetitive (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
      623 ∃ (μ : Randomized R.reveal) (α : ℝ), ∀ x,
      624 (∀ a ∈ μ.algorithms, P.feasible x (a.2 x)) ∧
      625 ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ → (μ.cost x : ℝ) ≤ ρ x * P.cost x τ + α
      626
      627/-- No deterministic algorithm is `ρ'`-competitive for a constant `ρ' < ρ`. -/
      628def DetLowerBound (ρ : ℝ) : Prop := ∀ ρ' < ρ, ¬ DetCompetitive R (const ρ')
      629
      630/-- No randomized algorithm is `ρ'`-competitive for a constant `ρ' < ρ`. -/
      631def RandLowerBound (ρ : ℝ) : Prop := ∀ ρ' < ρ, ¬ RandCompetitive R (const ρ')
      632
      633/-- For some `c > 0`, no deterministic algorithm is `c f`-competitive. -/
      634def DetLowerBoundFn (f : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
      635 ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ¬ DetCompetitive R fun x => c * f x
      636
      637/-- For some `c > 0`, no randomized algorithm is `c f`-competitive. -/
      638def RandLowerBoundFn (f : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
      639 ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ¬ RandCompetitive R fun x => c * f x
      640
      641-- Online, kept weight
      642
      643/-- A deterministic algorithm with ratio `ρ ≥ 1` and additive constant `α` for
      644the kept weight: every feasible schedule keeps at most `ρ` times what the
      645algorithm keeps, plus `α`. -/
      646def CompetitiveKeptR (total : Parameter P) (A : Algorithm P) (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) (α : ℝ) : Prop :=
      647 ∀ x, P.feasible x (A x) ∧ ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ →
      648 (total x : ℝ) - P.cost x τ ≤ ρ x * ((total x : ℝ) - P.cost x (A x)) + α
      649
      650/-- Some non-anticipative deterministic algorithm is `ρ`-competitive for the
      651kept weight. -/
      652def DetCompetitiveKept (total : Parameter P) (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
      653 ∃ A α, NonAnticipative R.reveal A ∧ CompetitiveKeptR total A ρ α
      654
      655/-- A distribution over non-anticipative algorithms is `ρ`-competitive for the
      656kept weight, in expectation. -/
      657def RandCompetitiveKept (total : Parameter P) (ρ : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
      658 ∃ (μ : Randomized R.reveal) (α : ℝ), ∀ x,
      659 (∀ a ∈ μ.algorithms, P.feasible x (a.2 x)) ∧
      660 ∀ τ, P.feasible x τ → (total x : ℝ) - P.cost x τ ≤ ρ x * ((total x : ℝ) - μ.cost x) + α
      661
      662/-- No deterministic algorithm is `ρ'`-competitive for the kept weight, for a
      663constant `ρ' < ρ`. -/
      664def DetLowerBoundKept (total : Parameter P) (ρ : ℝ) : Prop :=
      665 ∀ ρ' < ρ, ¬ DetCompetitiveKept R total (const ρ')
      666
      667/-- No randomized algorithm is `ρ'`-competitive for the kept weight, for a
      668constant `ρ' < ρ`. -/
      669def RandLowerBoundKept (total : Parameter P) (ρ : ℝ) : Prop :=
      670 ∀ ρ' < ρ, ¬ RandCompetitiveKept R total (const ρ')
      671
      672/-- For some `c > 0`, no deterministic algorithm is `c f`-competitive for the
      673kept weight. -/
      674def DetLowerBoundFnKept (total : Parameter P) (f : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
      675 ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ¬ DetCompetitiveKept R total fun x => c * f x
      676
      677/-- For some `c > 0`, no randomized algorithm is `c f`-competitive for the kept
      678weight. -/
      679def RandLowerBoundFnKept (total : Parameter P) (f : P.Inst → ℝ) : Prop :=
      680 ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ¬ RandCompetitiveKept R total fun x => c * f x
      681
